findings.text: `index_writing_form` matches `describe`'s work-tree forms by exact token against a fixed set (worker_git_shim.py:335 and :359-365), while git accepts any unambiguous abbreviation of a long option. Measured through the shim at head 4ec87830 against a foreign checkout left stat-stale backwards: `describe --di --long`, `--dirt --long` and `describe --di=<mark>` were forwarded and moved that checkout's index (rc=0, index bytes changed); only the full spellings `--dirty` and `--dirty=<mark>` refuse (rc=97, index unchanged). The real-git arms are the positive control, so the reading is not a spelling git ignored: the same four spellings without the shim all read rc=0 with the index moved, and `--d` is rejected rc=129 as ambiguous between --debug and --dirty. This is the same artifact, in the same class, that the hunk closes for the full spelling; and the parametrised sweep cannot see it, because every case in _INDEX_FORM_CASES (tests/test_git_shim_checks_the_resolved_repo.py:628) spells the option in full and the per-verb case built at :665 runs one fixed invocation, so the 151-test gate is green while the escape lives. `--dirty` is describe's only index-refreshing option, so the gap is the spelling, not a missing verb.

justifications.fit: the refusal reuses the module's resolve-then-compare shape and its REFUSAL_STATUS, extending the guard it repairs rather than adding a parallel mechanism; the extension carries the module's exact-token comparison into the one place where git's abbreviation grammar defeats it, and the shape the module already has for mixed verbs — an explicit reading form per verb — is what would close it.
